title: Rivercell launches with USD 25m to develop AI virtual-cell models for drug discovery
key_facts: Paris-based Rivercell emerged from stealth with a USD 25 million seed round led by HV, with HCVC, Alven and Bpifrance Digital Venture.
It is developing AI models to predict how human cells respond to drugs and genetic modifications, called the AI Virtual Cell (AIVC) model.
It is building a proprietary experimental platform to generate large time-resolved, multimodal single-cell datasets, aiming at the lack of data on how cells respond to interventions over time.
Targets: oncology, immunology, rare diseases and cardiometabolic conditions.
Funds will expand its automated wet lab in Paris and its data infrastructure.
CEO Yann Fleureau co-founded Cardiologs (bought by Philips in 2021); Chief Science Officer Eric Durand is ex-Novartis and ex-Owkin and co-founded Bioptimus.
Launch comes as a USD 1.8 billion virtual-cell initiative involving Biohub, the US Department of Energy, the NIH and major AI companies was announced.
quote_evidence: Rivercell is building a proprietary experimental data platform to generate large-scale, time-resolved, multimodal single-cell datasets, which will be used to train its AI Virtual Cell (AIVC) model.
The funding will support expansion of Rivercell's automated wet lab in Paris, scaling of its data generation infrastructure, and development of the AIVC model.
why_it_matters_hint: Seed-stage entrant in the race to model cells by computer.
